news.headline: Iraq PM targets militia stronghold in bid to assert state control

news.summary: US President Donald Trump warned US tech companies will face “a tremendous tax” if they build AI data centres abroad.

news.summary: The US president also spoke about the war in Iran and praised trip to China during a wide-ranging news conference.

news.headline: Two Salvadoran soldiers killed in Haiti while handling explosives
news.summary: Two others were injured in the explosion, marking the first deaths among troops deployed to Haiti since late October.

news.headline: Can the UK and EU turn the page on Brexit?
news.summary: A decade after the Brexit vote, the UK and EU have struck deals. But divisions persist.

news.headline: Gaza’s displaced children celebrate World Children’s Day
news.summary: Displaced children gathered in al-Nuseirat refugee camp to mark World Children’s Day.

news.summary: War forces schools, rehabilitation centres to close, forcing children with disabilities to lose access to education.

news.summary: Tallinn's decision to shut road border crossings comes after an attack on a drone manufacturer.

news.summary: Drones cause 'fear and panic' among Palestinians as Israel continues attacks on the Strip despite 'ceasefire'.

news.headline: Nepali cricket fans in Qatar want to see their team competing with the best
news.summary: As thousands from Qatar's Nepali community watch their team play, they hope that the team will rise in global rankings.

news.summary: Israeli-backed Palestinian militias accused of expanding operations, raising concerns over their role in Gaza’s security

news.headline: Indian man sentenced to 19 years in US Sikh separatist assassination plot
news.summary: Nikhil Gupta jailed for conspiring to hire a hitman to kill New York-based Sikh leader, Gurpatwant Singh Pannun.

news.headline: Nepal cricket fans celebrate their team’s global rise
news.summary: Nepal’s cricket fans have witnessed a transformation in their national team’s fortunes in recent years.

news.headline: Belgrade mayor charged with assaulting opposition politician in Serbia
news.summary: Prosecutors say Aleksandar Sapic caused serious facial injuries to a female councillor and seek a three-year sentence.

news.summary: Verdict against Myanmar may have implications for Israel's genocide in Gaza.

news.headline: Former US national security adviser confronted by students on Gaza
news.summary: Former US National Security Adviser Jake Sullivan was confronted by student protesters during a speaking event at MIT.

news.summary: Palestinian children gathered along Gaza’s coast for swimming lessons, finding relief from the psychological toll of war

news.headline: Ukraine strikes Kerch Bridge as Putin ally declares ‘no one needs Europe’
news.summary: Russia-Europe tensions rise as Ukraine uses its own weapons and communications tech to hit the Kerch Bridge.

news.headline: Zohran Mamdani unveils plan to close New York’s Rikers Island jail by 2032
news.summary: The plan would replace the jail complex with four smaller jails and reduce the number of people behind bars.

news.headline: US tech sell-off continues as Anthropic tumbles after mega IPO
news.summary: Anthropic's listing had been viewed as a potential boost for an industry struggling to regain its footing.

news.headline: West Bank: Record settler attacks mar olive harvest as UN urges Israel to protect farmers
news.summary: Israeli settlers have carried out more than 400 attacks causing casualties or property damage during this year’s olive harvest in the occupied West Bank – more than in any previous season, UN agencies and humanitarian NGOs said on Friday.

news.headline: Shattered playgrounds and freezing classrooms: Inside Ukraine’s deadliest year for children
news.summary: Amid the ruins of a twice-bombed Kyiv kindergarten as a day-long power cut continued, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) on Friday highlighted the dangers to youngsters enduring another brutal winter in Ukraine, as child casualty numbers rise to record levels.

news.headline: Afghanistan restrictions prevent pregnant women from seeking medical help
news.summary: Aid and development agencies in Afghanistan warned on Friday of an escalating “assault” on the rights and freedoms of women and girls that is preventing growing numbers from accessing vital medical care.&nbsp;

news.headline: Battle to control GPS and radio signals raises civilian safety concerns
news.summary: From aid convoys in conflict zones to passenger jets and cargo ships far out at sea, safe journeys depend on GPS, satellite navigation and old-fashioned radio transmissions. But these signals are increasingly being blocked or faked – and civilians are paying the price.

news.headline: Peacekeeping: With 500 paternity and child support claims unresolved, UN scales up accountability
news.summary: The UN is adding new accountability measures to better support children fathered by peacekeepers, the&nbsp;Under-Secretary-General for Management Strategy, Policy and Compliance, Catherine Pollard,&nbsp;announced Thursday.&nbsp;

news.headline: World’s top court finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya
news.summary: The International Court of Justice, the principal judicial organ of the UN, delivered its judgment on Thursday in the case of The Gambia v. news.headline: Dozens more children killed in Yemen amid escalating hostilities
news.summary: The UN child rights agency, UNICEF, on Wednesday called for warring parties in Yemen to protect children as renewed conflict between Houthi rebels and Government forces approaches the three-month mark.

news.headline: Patients running out of options as antibiotics stop working against common infections
news.summary: Common bacteria are becoming highly resistant to front-line and even “last-resort” antibiotics, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) said on Wednesday, warning that the situation today is worse than it was in 2019.&nbsp;

news.headline: Ukraine: Civilian casualties in 2026 already far exceed previous years’ tolls
news.summary: This year has seen dramatically higher civilian casualties in Ukraine than any other year since the full-scale invasion of the eastern European country by Russia in February 2022, the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine (HRMMU) said on Tuesday.&nbsp;

news.headline: Haiti: ‘Atrocious abuses’ continue as UN warns anti-gang operations must priortise civilian protection
news.summary: The UN human rights office, OHCHR has urged greater protection for civilians in Haiti amid ongoing “atrocious abuses” committed by gangs and intensified security operations.

news.headline: ‘Hunger should not be a concern’: WFP steps in for families in Kenya who fled Ethiopia violence
news.summary: The World Food Programme (WFP) is assisting&nbsp;thousands&nbsp;of families who fled recent violence in Ethiopia for the Moyale area in neighbouring Kenya, the UN agency reported on Tuesday.&nbsp;

news.headline: Winter rains deepen Gaza crisis amid restricted access and aid cuts
news.summary: Gaza is facing a deepening shelter, sanitation and food security crisis as winter rains flood makeshift shelters, destroy scarce food supplies and leave displaced families struggling to stay warm and fed.&nbsp;

news.headline: Lebanon leading the way in mental health support
news.summary: Mental health support must be a core part of the humanitarian response, said the UN Deputy Secretary-General during a visit to Lebanon over the weekend,&nbsp;where efforts to address the psychological toll of years of conflict and instability offer valuable lessons for other crisis-affected coun

news.headline: Syria: Progress ‘real’ but fragile, as remnants of war wreck young lives
news.summary: Syria is showing “undeniable signs of progress” nearly two years after the fall of the Assad regime, but explosive ordnance, the approaching winter and severe funding shortfalls threaten those fragile gains, senior UN officials told the Security Council on Monday.

news.headline: Guterres calls for a legally binding instrument for ‘killer robots'
news.summary: Talks began in Geneva&nbsp;on Monday to push for controls on lethal autonomous weapons systems that are often referred to as “killer robots”.

news.headline: At his final ASEAN Summit, Guterres upholds cooperation and action on Myanmar
news.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres underscored the need for stronger collaboration with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and an end to the crisis in Myanmar, in remarks to regional leaders meeting in the Philippine capital Manila on Monday.&nbsp;

news.headline: Nadia Murad: ‘Day by day, I took my story back’
news.summary: Nobel Peace Prize laureate Nadia Murad has spent years telling the world about the atrocities committed against her and the Yazidi community by militants from the terrorist group, ISIL.&nbsp;

news.headline: First Person: Managing risk on Ukraine’s frontline
news.summary: Humanitarian workers providing support to communities on the frontline of the war between Ukraine and Russia must balance remaining close to those in need with the heightened risks of operating in a warzone, according to the top UN official in Ukraine.

news.headline: When the rains fail: Preparing for drought in Central America
news.summary: Across Central America’s so-called Dry Corridor, farming families live at the mercy of the rains. In southwestern Honduras, Anastacio Martínez Gómez has spent most of his 73 years learning to work the land. But experience can only take him so far.

news.headline: Security Council LIVE: Fragile Gulf calm tested as threats to Hormuz shipping mount
news.summary: Nearly nine months after Israeli and US strikes on Iran set off a regional war, the Gulf remains on a knife edge. Iran has all but closed the Strait of Hormuz, which carried a fifth of the world’s oil before the conflict. Attacks on shipping are rising, and efforts to stop a return to full-scale fig

news.headline: DR Congo Ebola outbreak: Unrest fuelled by armed groups holds back response
news.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) continues to spread amid repeated and ongoing deadly attacks on civilians and frontline health workers by armed groups that are obstructing efforts to stop transmission, UN responders said on Friday.

news.headline: ‘Lives are at stake’: Humanitarians call for swift entry of winter supplies in Gaza
news.summary: Winter supplies must enter the Gaza Strip where “lives are at stake”, the UN and partners said in an urgent appeal on Friday, in the wake of deadly rainfall this past weekend.&nbsp;

news.headline: ‘Here, you can eat until you’re full’: Oleshky evacuees savour first proper meals in years
news.summary: In a quiet hospital corridor in Kyiv, staff and volunteers push carts carrying steaming pots of chicken soup, bread and buckwheat porridge to patients recently evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky, in Ukraine’s southern Kherson region.

news.headline: Six killed in Israeli airstrike on Gaza’s Nasser Hospital
news.summary: An Israeli airstrike on Gaza’s Nasser Hospital on Wednesday night killed six people, injured 27 others and caused extensive damage.&nbsp;

news.headline: Haiti: More than 1,000 killed between July and September, UN report reveals
news.summary: More than 1,000 people were killed in Haiti during the third quarter of this year, as armed gangs continue to terrorize the population in the capital Port-au-Prince and beyond, the UN team in the island nation, said in its latest human rights report.

news.headline: Aid is the ‘only hope’ for millions in Sudan, WFP chief warns, as funding cuts deepen hunger crisis
news.summary: The World Food Programme’s (WFP) new Executive Director has warned that funding cuts are worsening Sudan’s hunger crisis following his first field mission to the country, where he met families displaced by conflict and struggling to feed their children.&nbsp;

news.headline: Kenya begins countdown towards end of Ebola after last patient discharged
news.summary: Kenya began a 42-day countdown to the end of its Ebola outbreak on Thursday, a day after the last patient being treated for the disease went home and 11 people were released from quarantine.

news.headline: Lebanon: Devastation awaits returnees as UN peacekeepers prepare exit
news.summary: The situation in southern Lebanon remains volatile and extremely difficult for communities trying to rebuild their lives, UN peacekeepers based there report, despite a significant decrease in hostilities following an agreement in June between the United States, Lebanon and Israel.&nbsp;

news.headline: Egypt: Fact-checking site’s entire newsroom jailed as assault on press freedom widens
news.summary: Six journalists who make up the entire newsroom of the Egyptian fact-checking website Matsadash remain in detention, the UN human rights office (OHCHR) said on Tuesday, warning of proliferating assaults on press freedom by the Government.

news.headline: Nearly 64,000 flee Nigeria for Niger where a humanitarian crisis is deepening
news.summary: Violence in northern Nigeria is fueling a growing humanitarian crisis across the whole region: 64,000 have fled to neighbouring Niger and several hundred have left for Benin since the start of the year, as host countries struggle to cope, the UN’s refugee agency (UNHCR) said on Tuesday.&nbsp;

news.headline: Security Council LIVE: South Sudan’s first elections loom amid rising violence
news.summary: With South Sudan just six weeks away from its first national elections since independence, the Security Council meets in New York Tuesday amid deepening political uncertainty and worsening violence. Ambassadors are expected to press for an inclusive process and credible polls, while civilians bear t

news.headline: When deaths go uncounted: WHO flags dangerous blind spots in Africa’s health data
news.summary: Quality health data can help authorities to identify emerging threats and take lifesaving action, but a new report reveals critical gaps in Africa’s health information systems.&nbsp;

news.headline: Sudan war: First ‘suicide’ drone attacks, now long-range strikes are the norm
news.summary: Drones and drought are “closing in” on Sudan, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF), said on Tuesday, describing unprecedented attacks on the country’s infrastructure including by drones travelling up to 1,500 kilometres before hitting their target.

news.headline: Families who fled Ethiopia for Kenya’s Moyale need food, water and shelter
news.summary: The International Organization of Migration (IOM) and partners are calling for urgent funding to support tens of thousands of people who have escaped violent clashes in Ethiopia for the Moyale region in northern Kenya.

news.headline: Security Council LIVE: Strikes on Ukraine’s power grid, as peace talks loom
news.summary: The Security Council met in New York on Ukraine Monday. Russian strikes on energy infrastructure are threatening millions with another cold, dark winter, and civilian deaths are climbing sharply. news.headline: ‘For the first time I have my own chair’: Gaza siblings find new freedom
news.summary: In Gaza, 10-year-old Anas is one of three siblings born without legs and with only two fingers on each of their hands. They struggle to move around and perform daily activities like eating and writing independently.&nbsp;

news.headline: Sudan’s suffering is plain for all to see say aid teams, as brutal war continues
news.summary: Aid teams working to help millions of people uprooted by the ongoing war in Sudan appealed on Friday for more international assistance amid desperate funding shortages, empty warehouses and overwhelming needs.&nbsp;

news.headline: Abyei: Deadly drone strikes mark ‘new and concerning’ threat, UN peacekeeping chief warns
news.summary: Drone strikes that killed at least 30 people in Abyei last month have added “a new and concerning dimension” to security in the disputed area, the UN’s peacekeeping chief told the Security Council on Thursday.

news.headline: Two new Ebola vaccines to join DR Congo clinical trial
news.summary: Two new Ebola vaccine candidates will be added to a clinical trial in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) as the country continues to battle a deadly outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo species of the virus.&nbsp;&nbsp;

news.headline: Gunfire damages tents at Rafah displacement site in Gaza, as aid teams prepare for winter storms
news.summary: Gunfire hit and damaged multiple tents at a displacement site in Gaza’s northern Rafah region on Tuesday, reportedly causing injuries and forcing a humanitarian partner to leave the area, the UN aid coordination office (OCHA) has&nbsp;said.

news.headline: Syria’s undocumented children ‘pay the price’ of war and a law that shuts out mothers
news.summary: Many children born in Syria since the war began in 2011 have no legal identity because nationality passes only through fathers – many of whom are dead or missing – a member of the independent UN commission investigating rights violations in the country said on Wednesday.

news.headline: Afghan children face narrowing path to education, UN agencies report
news.summary: More than half of Afghanistan’s children who should be in primary school remain outside formal learning and millions of girls can only dream of going to university.

news.headline: Married off at 14: In Yemen’s war, women and girls suffer ‘devastating consequences’
news.summary: Safa is 14. Her mother died earlier this year. She has no brothers or sisters. And a few weeks ago, as the crisis took hold, her father married her to an elderly man, afraid that if he were killed in the hostilities, no one would be left to protect her.

news.headline: ‘This is not about politics. This is about people’: UN warns of impact of deadly drone strikes in Sudan
news.summary: Intensifying drone attacks on civilian infrastructure across Sudan are disrupting electricity, water and fuel supplies, putting lives at risk and hampering the delivery of humanitarian aid, the UN’s top official in the country has warned.&nbsp;

news.headline: Air raid alerts and attacks on schools: the devastating face of education in Ukraine
news.summary: Ukraine has sustained almost 2,000 attacks on education since the full-scale Russian invasion in 2022, with some 270 this year alone, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) said on Tuesday, a day after a strike at a school being used to distribute aid.

news.headline: Ethiopia: Violence in the north is pushing health system to the brink, WHO chief warns
news.summary: The head of the World Health Organization (WHO) called on Monday for greater protection for civilians caught in conflict in northern Ethiopia following deadly drone strikes this past weekend.

news.headline: Ukraine: WFP provides hot meals to Oleshky evacuees as UN pushes to restore power before winter
news.summary: The UN World Food Programme (WFP) is providing emergency food assistance to more than 400 people who were able to leave the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, in Ukraine’s Kherson region, during a brief local ceasefire.&nbsp;

news.headline: Western Sahara: UN ‘stands ready’ to keep supporting peace efforts as MINURSO mission ends
news.summary: The UN remains committed to supporting a just, lasting and mutually acceptable political solution in Western Sahara that provides for the self-determination of its people, Secretary-General António Guterres said on Sunday, as the UN peacekeeping mission there began to wind down.

news.headline: ‘They deserve to know the truth’: UN rights chief demands probe into staffer’s death in Houthi custody
news.summary: The UN human rights chief on Saturday demanded an independent investigation into the death of a Yemeni colleague held by the Houthis for more than two years, whose family learned of his death only weeks after it happened.

news.headline: Somalia looks to the future as the UN's political mission closes
news.summary: “The story of the UN's political engagement in Somalia has been one of persistence, partnership and adaptation,”&nbsp;Raisedon Zenenga, the UN Secretary-General's Deputy Special Representative for Somalia has said, as three decades of UN political missions in the Horn of Africa country

news.headline: Samarkand: A ‘living museum’ on the Silk Road grapples with a tourism boom
news.summary: As the sun sets over Samarkand’s majestic Registan, its last rays glint across the turquoise mosaics. Dusk settles on the ancient square where great trade routes have crossed for centuries.

news.headline: DPR Korea: Isolation deepens even as the country changes, says UN rights official
news.summary: The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) is building factories and hospitals, rolling out smartphones and mobile banking, and passing new laws at an unprecedented rate. But its people are more cut off from the outside world than at any point in the country’s history.

news.headline: UN rights office warns of deepening displacement ‘nightmare’ in Gaza
news.summary: Israeli forces continue to push Palestinians into ever-smaller areas of the Gaza Strip while destroying civilian infrastructure and attacking displacement sites, the UN human rights office, OHCHR, warned on Friday amid concerns of ethnic cleansing.&nbsp;

news.headline: Yemen war makes reaching assistance too dangerous for many
news.summary: More than 280,000 people have now been displaced by fighting in Yemen and many vulnerable people are unable to access lifesaving relief because it is too dangerous to do so, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) said on Friday.

news.headline: DR Congo: Hunger deepens for millions amid conflict, Ebola and climate shocks
news.summary: More than 28 million people in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) are not getting enough to eat and the number is expected to tick up in the coming months, according to the latest alert from the IPC global food security monitor.&nbsp;

news.headline: Ukraine: Oleshky ceasefire offers ‘hope’ for civilians as attacks on aid vehicles continue
news.summary: Each day the ceasefire in Oleshky holds means hope for civilians in the city, the UN’s top humanitarian official said, stressing that those wishing to leave must be able to do so safely and voluntarily.

news.headline: Myanmar’s illicit economy fuels escalating violence, with civilians bearing the brunt
news.summary: Myanmar’s human rights situation is “catastrophic”, the&nbsp;UN independent expert on the country warned at a press briefing Thursday, as the war spirals with no end in sight.&nbsp;

news.headline: Afghanistan opium production jumps fivefold as farmers find ways round Taliban ban
news.summary: Opium production in Afghanistan has risen fivefold in a year. According to a UN survey released on Thursday, it’s the first significant increase since the Taliban banned poppy cultivation in 2022.

news.headline: Civilians in Sudan’s El Obeid trapped between drones and incarceration
news.summary: Civilians in Sudan’s El Obeid live in constant fear of drone attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and of a wave of arbitrary arrests by the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), UN-appointed independent investigators said on Wednesday.&nbsp;

news.headline: DR Congo: WHO urges sustained efforts as Ebola cases top 10,000
news.summary: As Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) surpass the 10,000 mark, the World Health Organization (WHO) has underlined the need for continued efforts to contain spread of the disease.&nbsp;

news.headline: Higher Ground: How New York is raising a park to hold back the sea
news.summary: On 29 October 2012, Hurricane Sandy slammed into New York City, unleashing a devastating storm surge that flooded homes, subways and tunnels, knocked out power and sparked deadly fires.&nbsp;

news.headline: Backing for UN call to end Cuba embargo falls to 20-year low
news.summary: The UN General Assembly on Wednesday called for the 34th time for an end to the US economic, commercial and financial embargo on Cuba – but with the weakest backing for the resolution in two decades.

news.headline: Gaza: Families brace for fourth winter in tents as aid operations remain stymied
news.summary: Families in Gaza are bracing for a fourth winter in tents and makeshift shelters as UN aid operations face mounting obstacles, with transport suspended on Tuesday due to Israel’s closure of the key Kerem Shalom crossing for election day.&nbsp;

news.headline: Ebola: 20 contacts released from quarantine in Kenya, amid vaccine ‘hope’ in DR Congo
news.summary: Twenty people associated with Kenya’s first case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease have been reunited with their families after being released from quarantine following completion of a mandatory 21-day monitoring period.&nbsp;

news.headline: General Assembly weighs US embargo against Cuba ahead of 34th vote
news.summary: The General Assembly opened its annual debate on the US economic embargo against Cuba on Tuesday. On Wednesday, 28 October, Member States will vote for the 34th time on a resolution calling for it to end.

news.headline: West Bank: Hebron crackdown displaces thousands, Türk warns of ethnic cleansing
news.summary: Israel’s “aggressive operation” in the West Bank city of Hebron raises serious concerns of ethnic cleansing, UN human rights chief Volker Türk warned on Monday, as the number of Palestinians forced from their homes passed 3,000 on the eve of Israeli elections.

news.headline: Ukraine: Investigators find Russia committed war crimes by targeting civilians
news.summary: Top human rights experts investigating Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine&nbsp;said on Monday that the Russian authorities had committed war crimes and crimes against humanity by attacking civilians and vital energy infrastructure, among other violations of international law.

news.headline: West Bank: Guterres alarmed as Israel imposes sweeping closures after deadly Hebron attack
news.summary: The UN said on Friday it was “extremely alarmed” by intensifying violence in the occupied West Bank, as Israel moved to seal off the territory following a deadly attack on its soldiers in Hebron.

news.headline: Yemen: Deepening concerns for Taiz City as aid is blocked from entering
news.summary: Aid agencies warned on Friday of the fast-developing humanitarian emergency inside Taiz City in Yemen, which has been encircled by de facto Houthi forces fighting government troops along the country’s west coast.

news.headline: First human case of Shamonda virus reported in France as patient dies
news.summary: A patient in France has died after being infected with Shamonda virus, the first recorded human case of the disease.

news.headline: Migrants paid up to $500 million in smuggling fees on European sea routes
news.summary: The price tag for smuggling on European sea routes reached up to half a billion dollars last year, the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) and the UN migration office, IOM, reported on Wednesday.

news.headline: Fate unknown of many returned to DPR Korea from China: UN independent experts
news.summary: Three years on from the reported resumption of large-scale forcible returns of nationals of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) from China, serious concerns persist about their fate, according to a group of Human Rights Council-appointed independent experts.

news.headline: ‘One step away from famine’: Inside Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
news.summary: Following extreme hunger warnings, a bitter reality is unfolding across Afghanistan: food is available, but remains inaccessible for millions of people.

news.headline: Haiti: Elections on hold as gangs adapt to security crackdown, Security Council hears
news.summary: Armed groups in Haiti are adapting to intensified security operations, stepping up reprisals against civilians and extending their reach into rural areas, the UN warned the Security Council on Monday.

news.headline: Inside the New York ‘time machine’ racing to save a century of sound and film
news.summary: “I tell my kids I work in a time machine,” said Rhony Dostaly. In a basement beneath Lincoln Center, the media preservation engineer rescues moments from the past. “I go back in time, and I grab elements, and I make them available for people today.”

news.headline: Ukraine: Civilian casualty rates among ‘deadliest’ in years, as energy attacks intensify
news.summary: Civilian casualties in Ukraine&nbsp;remain at record levels, with intensified Russian attacks in September continuing a pattern of harm in 2026 far exceeding previous years, UN human rights monitors in Ukraine said on Friday.

news.headline: Ukraine: Critical health supplies destroyed in ongoing Russian attacks
news.summary: Ongoing and deadly Russian attacks across Ukraine are causing serious healthcare disruption, with more than $1.5 million-worth of medicines and supplies destroyed in four separate strikes on warehouses used by the UN there since July.&nbsp;

news.headline: Afghanistan faces record hunger levels amid rampant rights violations
news.summary: Acute malnutrition and hunger in Afghanistan have reached the highest levels ever recorded, with 15.9 million people facing acute food insecurity and conditions set to worsen in the coming months, according to a global hunger monitor report released on Thursday.

news.headline: Haiti sanctions renewed: Starving the gangs of bullets
news.summary:
Haiti is living through one of the world’s most acute security crises.
Armed gangs control large parts of the capital, Port-au-Prince, and are pushing into rural areas, terrorising communities, killing people, committing rape and other sexual assaults, kidnapping for ransom and extorting individuals

news.headline: Colombia: UN independent experts call for Ecopetrol to provide reparations to victims of armed conflict
news.summary: UN independent experts welcomed on Wednesday&nbsp;a recent landmark corporate accountability ruling involving the Ecopetrol oil company by Colombia’s Special Jurisdiction for Peace, calling for reparations for victims.
